haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The new engine's output goes to the shadow store, tagged with engine and mode.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store and never charges.
haiku-low.q3: The shadow gate must pass, per the draft a 7-day streak with a 5,000-invoice minimum, which is still open. A person makes the move.
haiku-low.q4: On-call by hand, or automatically when new charge failures exceed 2 percent in any 10-minute window. Auto-rollback applies in both and new_only, the latter only before day 35.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Gates reset, the rollout returns to shadow, and the 7-day streak restarts from zero before the new engine can take over again.
haiku-low.q6: Rollback from new_only stops being possible at day 35, because usage events are kept only 35 days and reprocess needs them. Late-rollback behavior after expiry is undecided.
haiku-low.q7: Engines read billing_mode from the config service and do not guess a mode. Charging waits if it is unreachable. Handling of an invoice mid-process: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: Gate state is proposed for a versioned rollout record beside billing_mode. Forward moves are made by a person, and both-to-new_only stays shut if mismatches or sign-off are unmet.
haiku-low.q9: Component: NOT STATED. It measures new-engine charge failure rate per 10-minute window. Above 2 percent, auto-rollback starts at Fence.
haiku-low.q10: The new engine is fenced, so it makes no new charges. The old engine charges due, unrecorded periods only after the flip at step 5.
haiku-low.q11: Each charge is checked against the ledger and its idempotency key before it is made. Reconcile also checks the ledger against the provider.
haiku-low.q12: Billing is left at the last completed step, recorded in the rollout record. On-call re-runs from Fence, since every step is idempotent.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its invoices to the shadow store, and never charges.
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store and never charges.
sonnet.q3: The shadow gate must pass. The document says a 7-day consecutive-day streak and an invoice minimum (5,000, with the sum-versus-per-day basis still an open question) with nightly comparison mismatches under 0.1 percent (assumed). A person makes the move, one step, approving it. The gate checks are only displayed preconditions.
sonnet.q4: A new-charge failure rate above 2 percent in any 10-minute window starts an automatic rollback at Fence. It can happen in both and new_only (new_only only before day 35). Shadow never auto-rolls back.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only, with billing_mode written as old_only and the gates reset (streak counter to zero, invoice counts and sign-off to starting values). The rollout then returns to shadow and the 7-day count starts again from zero. A person must approve each forward step again, starting with old_only to shadow.
sonnet.q6: It stops being possible at day 35 in new_only. The usage event log keeps only 35 days, so the skipped events needed for Reprocess are gone. A rollback deadline earlier than day 35 is needed, and the case of a late rollback is undecided.
sonnet.q7: Engines read billing_mode from the config service. NOT STATED how workers learn of a change (polling or push). If the flag is unreadable, charging waits and the failure is paged. NOT STATED what happens to an invoice being processed at the moment of a change, apart from rollback rules: the flag is never flipped while any charge is in an unknown state, and the flip only comes after Fence and Drain.
sonnet.q8: Gate state (streak, invoice counts, 14-day count, Finance sign-off, new_only entry timestamp, rollback progress) is proposed to live in a versioned rollout record next to the flag in the config service. Nightly comparison results are kept as one row per day per customer set in their own store. Nothing stops promotion automatically. Forward moves are always made by a person, and the controller displays the gate checks as preconditions. If a gate is blocked, it stays shut. The flag and the record change together under compare-and-set.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED which component detects it. The document gives the condition: a new charge failure rate above 2 percent in any 10-minute window in both or new_only. When it is met, auto-rollback starts at Fence.
sonnet.q10: Reconcile identifies any due, unbilled invoice so the old engine picks it up after the flip. Nothing is charged twice and nothing dropped. The new engine is fenced, so it starts no new charges. The old engine charges any period that is due and not yet recorded in the ledger only after the Flip, when billing_mode is written as old_only.
sonnet.q11: Every charge carries an idempotency key checked before charging, and every charge is checked against the ledger. Reconcile checks the ledger against the provider for every billing period. The old engine charges only periods not yet recorded in the ledger, and at most one engine can charge a given billing period at a time.
sonnet.q12: Billing is not flipped. Rollback holds at Hold (unknown outcome at Drain, ledger/provider disagreement at Reconcile, or missing events or a reprocess error at Reprocess). The flag is not flipped silently. The rollout record holds the last completed step. On-call resumes by re-running from Fence, and every step is idempotent. For a crash at any step, it is the same: re-run from Fence.
